# The frame after the choice: what the new system must pass, where it stands, and the first blocker (D548, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

Written at the council's instruction after D544 (the work toward production goes on the new system; the old system stays the
running default until the new one passes its gates). Every line that is not Alex's own is marked as proposed. Nothing here
changes a gate, a line or a frozen piece.

## 0. Frame

- **Objective:** bring the new system (`clean-arch/`: Step 1 at configuration c8, Steps 2 and 3, the step that writes answer
  choices, the frozen judge) through the gates below, so that it can replace the running default. Alex's word overrides the
  choice and any gate at any time.
- **Reference system:** the old system as it runs (`poc/config/poc-v118.json`), kept as the default and as the comparison.
- **The ruler:** the frozen ruler stays as it is (D261); no further paid test on it (D482).
- **Budget:** about $18.43 of D439's $40 recorded (Claude's ceiling, not Alex's). D544's first checkpoint: $5 of further
  spending on this direction without a candidate that passes its prewritten small test returns the direction to the council;
  $0.0022 of it used.
- **Stops in force on the new system's pieces:** the step that writes answer choices is frozen as it ran in the fourth Stage A,
  with no further tuning on Alex's 44 theses and no fifth run on them (D426); Steps 2 and 3 are frozen (D427); no more sentence
  changes to Step 1 on the July articles (D473, D477); no theme or ladder change for the rental-price boundary (D477); the
  judge is frozen (D354). A new version of any of these is a council decision under D439, reviewed before any send.

## 1. The gates in force, in order (council round 7 of the cold thread)

| Order | Gate | Its lines, and whose | Where the new system stands | What is not yet written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The step that writes answer choices (Stage A) | Alex's (D400): no question other than the topic's, no part left unlisted, no outcome with no range or two, no unjustified refusal; 35 of 44 topics right in two of three attempts, 28 of them by written choices; the same favourable end, and the same due day for nine in ten | **Not passed.** July, 40 fresh topics: the four hard lines each missed by one or two attempts even on the favourable count; 32 right, 22 by written choices (the council's scaled diagnostic, 32 and 26, is not Alex's number). Fresh week, 7 topics: no refusal; the omitted-clause marks of D547 | nothing |
| 2 | The judge on the system's own questions (Stage B) | D428, against the baseline reading: unsupported amount answers at most five points above baseline; unsupported yes-or-no answers at most 5%; unsupported last answers at most 3 in 30, scaled; the design's completeness, coverage and control conditions | **Not passed** (2026-11-12): four qualifying controls with the needed material against eight required (question mismatches and missing material both contributed); the last-answer line missed on its strictest reading, 3 of 24 | nothing |
| 3 | End to end against the old system, and Step 2's checks in that run | D427, D431: after gate 1 and 2, both systems unseeded on the frozen reference, the same day, three runs each; Step 2: search at least 90%, clear wrong merges at most 2%, no later detail lost through grouping | **Still owed as an acceptance.** The July census (new 2, 1, 0; old 1, 1, 1 of seven graded questions) was exploratory | a complete numerical definition of "beats" |
| 4 | Use on unseen news | opened by Alex beside the existing gates (D484); it changes none of them by itself (D483). The lines in `ACCEPTANCE-DESIGN.md` (four in five big matters covered; at most one in five questions trivia or duplicate; nine in ten last answers supported; at most one in twenty cited statements wrong; no undelivered fact that would change an answer) are **proposed, not his** | **Not an accepted gate yet.** One week, one run, as evidence for its design: 2 of 5 matters (2 of 2 outside the financial lines D505 excludes), 1 of 7 trivia, 6 of 7 last answers supported by both reader families, three confirmed undelivered pairs | the lines; how D505 counts in coverage; the number of runs |
| 5 | Integration with production storage and the pages, and release | the whole path integrated and accepted on the product's own path before it replaces the default | **Not started** | its acceptance and its numbers |

## 2. The first blocker: worthwhile questions the step declines (gate 1, the count by written choices)

The bounded question the council set: **can a general, permitted change recover a worthwhile question the system declines,
without making it answer questions it should refuse?** Answered from the stored records alone
(`clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/reachability/RESULT.md` with its theme census; `CHOICES-FOR-ALEX-2026-11-13.md`; the status
page's record of D467 to D482).

**The population.** In July the step's first pass declined eleven of the 40 topics. Two blind readers agree on ten: six are
rightly declined (five matters; four of the six are topics the first step should not have opened: a completed stake, a stake
too small to matter, a background sentence, an outcome no public material settles; two are the survey question Alex ruled out,
D417); four are worth a question the article supports, on two matters. One is split. Reaching the scaled 26 needs all four and
no loss elsewhere.

| Lead | The mechanism on record | A general change? | What stands against it |
|---|---|---|---|
| the memory-price pair | the first step's shape of the topic: a rolling twelve months; a second figure (a bank's estimate of one rack's memory cost) that no public material settles | none on record that is permitted: two first-step candidates aimed at this class failed their lines (c15yc, c17), first-step sentence changes on these articles are stopped (D473, D477), and the answer-choice step declines a rolling window by Alex's own ruling (D417) | the stops themselves |
| the rental-price pair (one article) | the step's rule "a matter that no theme in the request's themes covers", applied to twelve themes shown by id and name only. The census: the same topic declined in 5 of 9 attempts and given choices in 4 (three under "Semiconductor cycle", one under another theme); memory prices go under "Semiconductor cycle" in every attempt, though that theme's stored watch list holds only industry revenue growth. Six topics in all were declined for coverage in 12 attempts, three of them given choices in other attempts | in principle: tell the step what each theme carries, so that coverage is decided against a definition and not a name | what a theme carries is a product definition in `poc/universe.json`, which the old system shares; its stored definition of that theme does not include prices, so showing it as it is would make the step decline prices more consistently, not less; the definition itself is the first of the three choices written for Alex on 2026-11-13, untested. D477 stopped a theme or ladder change for this boundary after the check that the question, where it was opened, was decisive in no judgement of that window. The Stage A readers had ruled these refusals right on the list as it stands |

**Upside and protection.** The rental-price pair is at most 2 of the 4 the scaled count needs (22 to 24 of 26). None of the six
right refusals is a refusal for theme coverage, so a change of what the themes carry would not by itself turn them into
questions; the three other topics declined for coverage (a lidar ban, the CPU-to-GPU ratio in inference, Huawei's chip output)
have never been read for whether they are worth a question.

**Answer: no candidate.** The records establish a mechanism for one of the two matters, and for that one the change is a
product definition already put to Alex and stopped by a council decision, worth at most half the gap, with nothing on record
that the recovered question would receive sound choices or matter to a judgement. For the other matter no permitted change
exists. On the stored evidence the count by written choices is not reachable by a permitted change to the answer-choice step:
its distance is set upstream, by the topics the first step opens (rightly refused ones, and the memory shapes).

# Can an affordable comparison tell the two systems apart? The sizing (D516, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

**Answer: at the proposed size the comparison may miss differences that matter, and its reliability cannot yet be calculated from the
stored readings. It was not run.** Under simple assumptions (independent answers, the fresh week's question counts, the shares seen
so far) the smallest difference such a comparison would detect four times in five is between about 22 and 38 points for the shapes
the money allows, and more if repeated draws add little; these are illustrations, not a measured boundary. The differences seen so
far are 6, 19 and 26 points on one run each, which neither establish the true differences nor rule out larger ones. By the stop
condition written in D516 this design is not sent. That stops this design at this size; it does not show that the systems are
equal, or that no comparison could ever decide.

Scripts: `draw_counts.py` (what each stored draw holds, by code; `draw-counts.json`), `sizing.py` (the calculation, its inputs printed
with their sources, the closed form checked by simulation).

## 1. What each reading has, per draw (nothing here is made comparable that is not)

| Reading | July window, 14 days (2026-07-01..14) | Fresh week (2026-09-22..28) | Draws of one system on the same news |
|---|---|---|---|
| Big matters covered, both teams (outside the company's own financial level) | trial, one draw each: new 6 of 7 (one team: the seventh missed; the other: folded into another question), old 7 of 7 | one draw each: new 2 of 2, old 1 of 2 | **none** |
| Questions that are trivia or duplicates, both teams | not read | one draw each: new 1 of 7, old 6 of 15 | **none** |
| Answers supported by what the judge was shown, both teams | trial, one draw each: new 7 of 9, old 10 of 12 | one draw each: new 6 of 7, old 10 of 15 | **none** |
| Cited statements whose summary departs from the passage the judge was shown (neither reading checked them against the full articles) | trial: 4 of 201 flagged by both teams (the two systems together, unconfirmed) | one in each system | none |
| Delivery (facts that reached the judge of their question) | trial, the gold's 62 facts, one draw each: delivered new 31, old 22; never delivered though judged later: new 8, old 19; no known "would change" control | the new system only: three confirmed pairs, 23 open (D508) | none |
| Agreement with the frozen reference, seven graded questions | **three draws each**: new 2, 1, 0; old 1, 1, 1 | not applicable | the only reader-based line with repeats: the new system's own spread (0 to 2) is wider than the gap between systems |
| By code: questions opened | new 9, 8, 12; old 12, 13, 14 | new 7; old 15 | three draws each in July |
| By code: statements with no question (new) | 347, 286, 310 of about 550 | 382 of 567 | three draws in July |
| By code: share of links on the largest question | new 0.20, 0.25, 0.20; old 0.53, 0.32, 0.39 | new 0.26; old 0.28 | July: the ranges do not overlap; the fresh week shows no gap |

Sources: `TRIAL-RESULT.md`; `week/WEEK-RESULT.md`; `clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/CENSUS-FULL-RESULT.md`; `draw-counts.json`.

What this table says before any calculation:
- For the three reader-based lines a choice would rest on (matters covered, question quality, answers supported) there is **one draw
  of each system on each of two windows, and no repeat**: the spread between draws of one system is unmeasured for them.
- Where repeats exist (the frozen reference; counts by code), a system's own spread is as wide as the gap between systems, except
  for the share of links piled on one question in July, and that gap is absent in the fresh week.
- On answers supported, the sign of the difference flips between the two windows (6 points for the old system, then 19 for the new).

## 2. How large a difference a comparison could detect

Inputs (all from the fresh week, and all estimates): at the end of one week the new system holds 7 questions with a latest answer
and the old system 15; a week costs about $2.52 a draw for the new system (charged) and about $0.50 for the old (its token count at
listed rates, rounded up; not a separately charged amount). The article database holds articles for three later weeks (2026-10-06
to 10-26); **no exposure census has been run on them and no article list priced**, so their being unread and their cost are
assumptions here. The week of 09-29 has 40 articles already read once by the reading step.

The smallest true difference detected four times in five (two-sided, 5%):

| Shape | Cost | Answers supported | Trivia or duplicates |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 week, 3 draws each | about $9 | 31 points if repeated draws were as good as new weeks; 54 if they add nothing | 34; 60 |
| 2 weeks, 3 draws each | about $18 | 22; 38 | 24; 42 |
| 3 weeks, 1 draw each | about $9 | 31 | 34 |
| 3 weeks, 2 draws each | about $18 | 22; 31 | 24; 34 |
| 4 weeks, 3 draws each (more unread news and money than there is) | about $36 | 16; 27 | 17; 30 |

- The calculation assumes independent answers, fixed weekly question counts and particular starting shares. Questions within a
  week, and repeated draws of the same week, are correlated to a degree the stored runs do not measure for these readings. "As good
  as new weeks" is an upper bound on what repeated draws can give.
- The simulation checks the formula under the same assumptions; it does not validate the assumptions. For 3 weeks and 1 draw (21
  and 45 answers): a 31-point difference is detected in 82% of 20,000 simulated comparisons, a 10-point difference in 12%, and a
  20-point difference in roughly 40 to 60% depending on the starting shares (about 37% at 83 against 63, about 57% at 97 against
  77, the council's own runs).
- Big matters covered cannot be sized this way at all: a week gives two to seven such matters.

## 3. The stop condition of D516, applied

- **A stated difference the comparison is meant to detect:** none can be defended. Under the simple assumptions the shapes the
  money allows detect differences of roughly 22 to 38 points or more; one draw of each system does not tell us whether the true
  differences are that large (the largest seen is 26 points, on one week), and on the one line with two windows the sign flips.
- **A defensible size and cost for it:** the reliability of a $9 to $18 comparison cannot be calculated from the stored readings
  (no repeated draws of the reader-based lines; correlation unmeasured). Spending the remaining money on a test whose power is
  unknown and plausibly low is not defensible.
- **The readers' controls:** the delivery reading still has no known single-fact "would change" case (the six calls of D511 did not
  give one), so that line could not be exercised either.
- **So this design is not sent.** What is unmeasured and would have to change for a comparison to decide: many more independent
  weeks of unread news than the database holds (seven to nine weeks for a 20-point difference at one draw each), or a line that does
  not depend on the handful of questions a week produces.

## 4. What this means for the decision page

The page's section 5 offered Alex "one comparison written down before it runs" as the way to choose by measurement. The page now
says, in plain words: at the proposed size the comparison may miss differences that matter; we cannot yet calculate its
reliability from our stored readings; we did not run it.

## 5. Council (reflection thread "my", round 7): consensus, with corrections

The council ran the script and reproduced its figures, and corrected this page's first wording: "only about 30 points or more" (the
table gives 22 to 38), "nothing seen suggests a 30-point difference" (one draw does not establish it), the single 40% figure for a
20-point gap (it depends on the starting shares), the row that claimed a check of cited statements against their articles (both
readings used the passages shown to the judge), and the unread weeks and costs stated as facts (they are estimates until an
exposure census and an article list exist). **Decided under D439 (D517): this comparison is not sent.**

third reader of each family (70 differing marks, 10 faults named under W). Count by `stage_a/collect_readings.py report` on
`poc/data/clean-e2e-full-2026-11-13/stage-a/` (the three draws' outcomes joined; report `stage-a/report.txt`, `stage-a-report.json`).

| line | every split ruling counted for the answer | counted against it |
|---|---|---|

| 2. no ladder fails L | missed: c3/clean-7 p1, c1/clean-5 p3 | missed: 3 |

**The faults behind the favourable count** (both third readers agree): a question that does not name the model it asks about (c3 credit

**Where the two third readers split (41 points), by class:** whether the H100 rental price is covered by the semiconductor-cycle theme

**Limits:** D400's limit holds: Stage A measures the step against the lines and its own three sends; it says nothing about production.

# Are the eleven first-pass refusals reachable? Two blind readers, $0 (D476), 2026-11-13

**Answer: of the eleven theses the judge's first pass refused on the full run, both readers agree on ten. Six should be declined: no
question worth asking in any shape the ladder step can take (five distinct matters). Four runs, two distinct matters, have a question
worth asking that the article supports in a shape that can be laddered: the H100 rental price (twice, from one article) and the memory
price (two articles). They split on one: federal AI obligations.** On this population Stage A counts 32 right, 22 by a written ladder,
of 40 (line scaled to 32 and 26). So the written line is reachable on paper only if all four agreed conversions land and nothing else is
lost: +4 gives 26.

Readers: Codex (`codex-phase1.jsonl`, `codex-phase2.jsonl`) and a Claude subagent (`claude-phase1.jsonl`, `claude-phase2.jsonl`). Each read
the article and the library at that step first, without the thesis, and wrote the questions the source supports (Codex 13, Claude 18:
12 distinct matters), then compared them with the thesis (`packet-phase2.json`); the key (`key.json`) was not shown.

| case | thesis | Codex | Claude | the mechanism behind the refusal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 5 | c1/clean-12, c3/clean-10: the H100 GPU-hour rental price in 2026 | reachable (as written for c1) | reachable (year-end price) | the ladder step's rule "a matter no listed theme covers" (`poc/universe.json` holds 12 themes, among them "AI capital spending" and "Semiconductor cycle"; the model judged that none covers a GPU rental price, and the Stage A readers split): not the thesis's shape |
| 7 | c1/clean-13: HBM/DRAM prices over the 12 months to mid-2027 | reachable (DRAM price, calendar 2026) | reachable (DRAM price, calendar 2026) | Step 1's rolling window (the period rule read as a horizon) |
| 8 | c2/clean-6: memory contract prices in 2026 and the rack's memory cost | reachable (DDR5 contract price, 2026) | reachable (DRAM contract price, 2026) | Step 1's second figure (a bank's rack estimate no public material settles) |
| 10 | c1/clean-15: federal AI obligations and potential awards | reachable (obligations, calendar 2026) | declining right (about $7bn cannot move NVIDIA's revenue: §4 test 1) | split |
| 2, 6 | c1/clean-10, c3/clean-9: the China domestic-share survey | declining right | declining right | D417 (Alex: "这类题不出题") |
| 3 | c2/clean-10: custom-ASIC spending against NVIDIA GPU purchases | declining right | declining right | no dated outcome the article supports (both); the Stage A readers had called this refusal wrong |
| 4 | c1/clean-2: the Intel stake's size and carrying amount | declining right | declining right | a completed, sized investment is not an obligation (§3 C) |
| 9 | c3/clean-3: US approval of China sales and their scale | declining right | declining right | one background sentence; no pending decision named |
| 11 | c1/clean-11: the Firmus investment and stake | declining right | declining right | about $500m cannot change NVIDIA's revenue, profit, cash or credit risk |

**What it shows.**
1. Most refusals are right, and for a reason upstream of the ladder: four of the six right refusals are theses Step 1 should not have
   opened at all (a completed stake, a small stake, a background sentence, an outcome with no settling material). The refusal is the
   pipeline catching Step 1's over-opening.
2. The reachable four come from two different places: two from a Step 4 rule (the H100 price refused because no theme in the fixed list
   covers it; Claude's reader called declining "wrong here"), two from Step 1's memory shapes (the same class c15yc and c17 failed on).
3. A restructure in which the opening step writes the ladder could touch at most the memory pair and the over-openings; it would not touch
   the theme-list refusals unless the opening step also stopped needing a listed theme.
4. Limits: one run's population; the readers judged worth and shape, not a written ladder's quality; the Stage A readers earlier ruled the
   H100 refusals right on the theme list as it stands (council round 5).

## Addendum: every theme-coverage decline in the stored final-configuration answers (council round 20's step 1, $0; `theme-census.txt`)

Read: the fourth Stage A run (132 answers) and the full run's three draws (120), every send. **Six theses were declined for "no listed theme
covers it" (12 sends), and the same model laddered three of them under an existing theme in other sends.** The H100 rental price: declined
in five of nine sends over the three draws and laddered in four: three under "Semiconductor cycle" (an annual average or a year-end price)
and one under "Custom silicon at cloud providers" as a yes/no on staying below the peak (c2 send 3; council round 21 caught the miscount). The other three:
a US lidar ban (two declines, once laddered under "Chip export controls", a wrong fit), the CPU-to-GPU ratio in inference (declined 3 of 3),
Huawei's chip output (two declines). 31 theses were laddered under a theme in 80 sends; memory prices go to "Semiconductor cycle" every time,
although that theme's definition (`poc/universe.json`) watches only industry revenue growth.

So the H100 refusal is not a missing theme or a new-theme path: it is the model's coin flip on whether a thinly defined existing theme
"covers" a market price, the same theme it stretches to memory prices without hesitation. A new-theme design (storage, deduplication,
cross-company reading, D191) is not needed to explain it; whether a theme's definition should name the prices it carries is a product
question about `poc/universe.json`, which production shares.

## Addendum 2: does the H100 thesis reach any judgement that matters? (council round 21's check, $0; corrected in round 22)

Only draw c2's first pass laddered it (c1 and c3 declined), so c2 is the one place to look. Its theme judgement (v8, "What is Ornn's
published H100 GPU-hour spot rental price … on December 31, 2026?", rung 3, $2 to below $3) was shown as theme context in 31 company-question
judge requests (`poc/data/clean-e2e-full-2026-11-13/c2/judge/draw-c2/archive.sqlite`). A first count searched the answers' text and found
none; the council found that **20 of the 31 answers cite it by id** in their structured theme pushes (a text search misses an id): five
questions, v1 credit support (5), v2 Vera Rubin shipments (5), v3 China's H200 authorization (1), v5 the Kyber rack (4), v7 supply commitments
(5); 18 push one way, 2 the other. Read in the last judgement of each: the reasons of v1, v2, v3 and v5 never mention the rental price; v7's
says "The updated lower-rental-price theme is a counterweight, but not enough to pull the estimate below the $125 billion boundary." By subject,
v3 and v5 are the questions behind graded q08 and q18; their reasons do not rest on it. No same-input control was run, so this shows no
decisive use in this window, not that the theme had no effect.

# The new system's position, and the choices left (D477), 2026-11-13

**In one line:** the new system is not ready to replace the current one, and further wording fixes on this test set no longer move it; what
is left are choices about how the product is built. (Checked by the council, round 23.)

## Where it stands

- **The step that writes each question's answer options**, on 40 questions, must get at least 26 right with options it wrote (scaled from your
  line of 28 of 44). It gets 22. Of the other 18, 10 are declines that the readers count as right, and 8 are wrong.
- **Why it declines (the 11 declines its first pass made, checked by two independent readers):** six are right, and four of those six are
  questions the first step should never have opened (a stake already completed, a $500 million stake too small to matter, a background
  sentence, a figure no public report will settle). In four, the article supports a question worth asking that could be given options: the
  H100 rental price twice (the step sometimes files it under the semiconductor-cycle topic and sometimes says no topic covers it) and the
  memory price twice (once the first step wrote "the 12 months to mid-2027" instead of one calendar year; once it tied the price to a bank's
  estimate of one rack's memory cost). On paper, fixing all four and losing nothing would give 26. That is arithmetic, not an expected result:
  the readers did not check that the replacement questions would get good options, and they are narrower than the originals.
- **What today's fixes did:** four wording changes to the first step (the year split, the identity rule, the calendar-year rule, the
  unsigned-deal rule) were tested, on stored articles and, for two of them, on unseen ones. None was adopted: each moved the error to a
  neighbouring question, made the model stop asking, or found the old version already doing it half the time. The model's answers to the same
  request also swing widely (one question opened 3 of 3 times in one test and 0 of 3 in another), so three tries per case cannot show small
  gains.
- **Spend:** about $27 of the $40 ceiling I set myself for this period; nothing committed or pushed.

## The choices

1. **Define the research topics more fully.** The list of world topics (`poc/universe.json`, shared with the current system) defines
   "semiconductor cycle" only by industry revenue growth. The model files memory prices under it every time; it filed the H100 rental price
   under it in 3 of 9 tries, under a wrong topic once, and declined 5 times. Naming what each topic carries might settle this; that is untested.
   Where the H100 question did get options, 20 later judgements referred to it and one said it pushed the other way "but not enough" to change
   its answer; whether it changes any final answer is unmeasured.
2. **Make the first step write the answer options itself**, so that a question it cannot give options to is, in intention, not opened in that
   shape. Untested. It could touch at most the two memory cases and the over-opened questions, not the H100 declines unless the topic rule also
   changes; like two earlier attempts, it may make the model stop opening hard questions. Its benefit, risk and cost would be designed and
   reviewed before any send.
3. **Put the effort back into the current system.** It stays the default either way; the new system's parts (search, comparison, grouping)
   remain built and frozen for later.

The council has made no choice among these: D477 records them for you and stops paid tests on the new system until a choice is made by you,
or by the council on new evidence.

Design: `RECORD-TEST-2-DESIGN.md` (version 2, frozen before the send). Tallies: `tally-record2.txt` (the six questions),
`tally-fidelity.txt` (the sampled lines). Record A is c22's (a source and a fixed-form period on each figure); record B is c8's (the
adopted request: one party per statement). The letters were drawn by seed; the readers and comparers never saw which was which.

## The verdict, by the lines written before the send

- **Record B (c8, the adopted request): meets the line.** Both of its readers: six questions exercised, five the same, one with an
  omission (Q6), no part wrong.
- **Record A (c22): undecided.** Both of its readers: Q1, Q3, Q4 and Q5 the same, no part marked wrong by both comparers; the marks on
  Q6 (both readers) and on Q2 (one reader) are split between the comparer families (one says wrong, the other incomplete or
  supported) and stayed split after a fresh comparer of each family.
- **The comparison the test was sent for is not shown.** c22's record did not let a reader answer more, or more rightly, than c8's.
  The wrong attribution that c8's record led to in the first record test (D494) did not recur on these forty articles: no reader of
  either record gave a figure to the wrong party on Q1 to Q5.

One draw an article, a constructed library, a screened sample, four record readers: a lead about these articles, not a general claim.

**I agree to prepare one more unseen week for a Stage A diagnostic, with the send conditional on a $0 exposure and cost check.** The result can help decide whether a larger acceptance is worth designing. It cannot by itself pass Stage A or establish that the rebuild cannot meet its gates.

For example, the fresh week had seven topics and no refusals across 21 attempts. July had eleven first-pass refusals among 40 topics. Those populations and news windows differ, so the contrast is a reason to investigate—not yet evidence that the problem has disappeared.

The **“no candidate” conclusion holds for the bounded question we asked**. The memory-price cases need changes to how the first step shapes the questions; the relevant attempts failed and further sentence changes on those articles were stopped. The rental-price cases expose uncertain theme coverage, but changing the shared theme definition was stopped for that boundary and is untested. The four possible recoveries are paper estimates, not demonstrated sound answers. D439 can open a new version by a further decision; the record does not prove that no future change is possible. [Frame](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md>), [reachability review](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/reachability/RESULT.md>)

I would correct the measurement plan in five places:

1. **Do not call unseen news Alex’s defined Stage A population.** D400 fixed lines for 44 topics and three attempts each; it did not establish this proposed sampling method. The new week is a diagnostic of the frozen step on different news. Any later acceptance population and use of the 44-topic lines need to be fixed before that acceptance.

2. **Make the exposure and price check a real stop.** Freeze a complete, ordered week only if every included article is shown not to have been sent by earlier runs or probes. Price the actual list and all components, attempts and independent readings before committing to the send. The earlier **$2.52** is the charge for a complete clean draw, including judging; it is a useful baseline, not a verified price for this week or for the proposed abbreviated run.

3. **Prove the abbreviated run before paying.** The current [runner](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/run_fresh.py>) runs the judge after answer choices; it has no ordinary “stop after choices” option. A bounded harness must prove, at $0, that it uses the same frozen steps and state, records all three attempts, and charges every paid attempt to the shared ceiling. If that proof is not available, do not silently substitute a different run.

4. **Fix the diagnostic rule before reading.** Require at least **14 pooled topics**, including the seven already read, with three attempts each; otherwise the result is inconclusive. As a *proposed diagnostic*, apply the four zero-fault lines, consistent direction, and at least 90% consistent dates; require at least `ceil(35 × topics / 44)` topics right in two of three attempts and `ceil(28 × topics / 44)` right with written choices. At 14 topics those counts are **12 and 9**. Report each week separately and show disputed readings and the existing fresh-week marks alongside any sensitivity treatment. These scaled numbers are not Alex’s acceptance lines.

5. **Do not make a reversal automatic.** If the diagnostic meets that proposed rule, the council can assess whether a properly sized acceptance is justified. If it misses, read the failures and their product effect before deciding whether there is a repair or whether the direction should change. Two weeks and roughly 14 topics do not establish that the unchanged gates are unattainable. The **$3.50 ceiling** must include the run and its readings; D544’s **$5 checkpoint** still returns the direction to the council under its stated condition.

The 40 later articles already sent to c8 for the financial-record test may still contain useful stored observations, although they used a constructed library and were selected for financial figures. They cannot count as unseen news for this run or as a full Stage A measurement. [Record test](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/record-2/RECORD-TEST-2-RESULT.md>)

Position: Prepare one unseen-week Stage A diagnostic; send only after the exposure, full cost and abbreviated-run checks pass, and treat its outcome as a decision lead rather than an acceptance or automatic reversal.
